message.content: Fusion research has benefited society by improving plasma science, materials engineering, and superconductors for medical tools. It has strengthened nuclear safety methods, because containment and diagnostics developed for fusion reactors help monitor fission plants more reliably. Superconducting magnets from fusion experiments are now used in MRI systems, particle accelerators, and research instruments that support science and medicine. Plasma physics findings from fusion studies have also informed controlled combustion, electric propulsion, and efficient manufacturing techniques. Although the iritic concept remains hypothetical, real fusion research educates engineers, protects energy infrastructure, and inspires long lasting clean power solutions.
